newsitem.title: USA: Video Update Q3 reflects new amortization.
newsitem.headline: Video Update Q3 reflects new amortization.

text.p: Video Update Inc, an international video retail chain, said results of its January 31, 1997 third quarter reflects the company's adoption of a new, more conservative method of amortizing videocassette rental inventory.

For the third quarter, it reported earnings of $0.12 per share, up from $0.10 per share in the 1996 fiscal third quarter. It said that if the fiscal 1996 quarter had reflected the new amortization method, net income (fully diluted) would have been $0.04 per share.

The company said same-store sales increased 11 percent in the third quarter of fiscal 1997 over the same year-ago period. As of January 31, Video Update had 290 company-owned stores, up from 194 at the same time last year. The company's same-store sales base includes 181 stores.

"The company remains on schedule with its aggressive growth strategy of acquiring and building new stores," said chairman Dan Potter in a statement. "In February, we increased our credit facility to $60 million. We believe this additional capital and our strong balance sheet keep us well positioned for the video rental industry's consolidation movement.

"In recent weeks, for example, we have completed the acquisition of a 23-store video retail chain in Alberta, Canada and a seven-store chain operating in Texas and Oklahoma," said Potter. "We also opened 19 new stores in the third quarter."
